name: TypeScript Production Systems Track
description: Master static typing, interfaces, generic programming, utility types, type narrowing, and architectural design patterns in modern TypeScript.
whatYouLearn: Master static type annotations and type inference
Define strict contract models with Interfaces and Type Aliases
Write reusable generic components, functions, and constraints
Leverage Utility Types (Pick, Omit, Partial, Record, Readonly)
Perform runtime type narrowing using custom type guards
Build a production-grade Type-Safe CLI Application
prerequisites: JavaScript ES6+ Full Stack Engine Track

exercises.title: Primitive Type Annotations & Type Inference
exercises.description: Annotate variables explicitly with boolean, number, string, and array types.
exercises.theory: TypeScript adds static typing to JavaScript. Explicit annotations ensure compile-time verification, while implicit inference infers types automatically from initial assignment.
exercises.objective: Add explicit static type annotations to variables and function parameters.
requirements: Annotate string, number, and boolean primitive types explicitly
Annotate string array type string[]
hints: Use syntax variableName: typeName = value
Array types can be written as string[] or Array<string>
exercises.codeExample: const name: string = 'Alex'; const age: number = 25;

exercises.title: Interfaces & Contract Specifications
exercises.description: Define object structure contracts using TypeScript interfaces with optional and readonly fields.
exercises.theory: Interfaces define data shape contracts. Mark optional fields with ? and immutable fields with readonly.
exercises.objective: Define a UserProfile interface with optional and readonly properties.
requirements: Create UserProfile interface
Mark id as readonly
Mark avatarUrl as optional string
hints: readonly prevents property mutation after initial object assignment
exercises.codeExample: interface User { readonly id: number; bio?: string; }

exercises.title: Type Aliases vs Interfaces
exercises.description: Model complex union types, primitive aliases, and tuple definitions.
exercises.theory: Type aliases (type Name =) can model primitives, unions, tuples, and function signatures, whereas interfaces excel at object contract extensions.
exercises.objective: Define type aliases for API Status union and Coordinate tuple.
requirements: Define Status string literal union type
Define Point tuple type [number, number]
Use type alias in ApiResponse object
hints: Unions represent one of several specified literal or type options
exercises.codeExample: type Status = 'pending' | 'active'; type Point = [number, number];

exercises.title: Function Signature Typing
exercises.description: Annotate function parameters, return types, default parameters, and void/never returns.
exercises.theory: Explicitly typing function arguments and return types prevents runtime type errors and enables IDE autocomplete.
exercises.objective: Annotate function parameters and return type explicitly.
requirements: Annotate amount as number and currency as string with default 'USD'
Explicitly annotate return type : string
Annotate void return type on logError
hints: void indicates function does not return a value
exercises.codeExample: const add = (a: number, b: number): number => a + b;

exercises.title: Enums (Numeric & String Enums)
exercises.description: Group related constants using string and numeric Enums.
exercises.theory: Enums allow defining named sets of related constants. String enums provide clear value representations in logs and database payloads.
exercises.objective: Model UserRole and LogLevel string enums.
requirements: Declare LogLevel string enum with INFO, WARN, and ERROR values
Use LogLevel as typed parameter in logMessage
hints: String enum members require explicit string values
exercises.codeExample: enum Role { ADMIN = 'ADMIN', USER = 'USER' }

exercises.title: Generics: Functions & Type Parameters
exercises.description: Write reusable generic functions that preserve type safety across arbitrary types.
exercises.theory: Generics <T> capture argument types dynamically, enabling reusable logic while preserving precise type checking.
exercises.objective: Write generic Identity and Array Wrapper functions.
requirements: Use generic type parameter <T>
Return generic array type T[]
Invoke with explicit type parameters <number> and <string>
hints: Type parameter T acts as a type placeholder resolved when function is called
exercises.codeExample: function identity<T>(arg: T): T { return arg; }

exercises.title: Generic Interfaces & Classes
exercises.description: Architect generic data storage repositories and API response wrappers.
exercises.theory: Generic interfaces and classes generalize data structures such as queues, stacks, and standardized API payload containers.
exercises.objective: Build a generic ApiResponse<T> interface and Repository<T> class.
requirements: Define generic interface ApiResponse<T>
Build generic class DataStore<T> with add and getAll methods
hints: Class type parameter <T> applies across constructor, fields, and class methods
exercises.codeExample: interface Response<T> { data: T; } class Store<T> {}

exercises.title: Generic Constraints (extends)
exercises.description: Restrict generic type parameters using the extends keyword.
exercises.theory: Generic constraints (<T extends Interface>) restrict valid generic type parameters to types possessing specific properties.
exercises.objective: Constrain a generic function to objects containing an length or id property.
requirements: Define HasId interface with id field
Constrain generic function with <T extends HasId>
Return T | undefined
hints: T extends HasId guarantees that item.id exists on any passed element
exercises.codeExample: function logLength<T extends { length: number }>(arg: T) { return arg.length; }

exercises.title: Type Narrowing & Custom Type Guards
exercises.description: Safely narrow union types using typeof, instanceof, and custom is type predicates.
exercises.theory: Type guards narrow broad union types within conditional blocks. Custom type predicates (pet is Dog) inform the compiler of custom validation logic.
exercises.objective: Write custom type guards for API error responses vs success payloads.
requirements: Define UserSuccess and UserError interfaces
Write custom type guard isSuccess returning response is UserSuccess
Demonstrate safe property access in handleResponse
hints: returnType is type syntax informs TS compiler that boolean true guarantees parameter type
exercises.codeExample: function isString(val: unknown): val is string { return typeof val === 'string'; }

exercises.title: Discriminated Unions (Tagged Unions)
exercises.description: Model complex state machines using tagged union patterns with a shared literal field.
exercises.theory: Discriminated unions share a common single-literal property (tag) across all union members, enabling exhaustive switch-case narrowing.
exercises.objective: Model a Redux-style action dynamic dispatcher using discriminated unions.
requirements: Create Action union with shared 'type' discriminant string tag
Write reducer function using exhaustive switch(action.type)
hints: TS automatically infers payload exists when action.type === 'FETCH_SUCCESS'
exercises.codeExample: type Shape = { kind: 'circle'; r: number } | { kind: 'square'; size: number };

exercises.title: Utility Types: Partial, Required & Readonly
exercises.description: Transform existing interface models using Partial<T>, Required<T>, and Readonly<T>.
exercises.theory: Built-in utility types perform global modifications: Partial<T> makes all properties optional, Required<T> forces all optional fields mandatory, and Readonly<T> freezes properties.
exercises.objective: Use Partial<T> for partial user update functions.
requirements: Define base Article interface
Use Partial<Article> for fieldsToUpdate parameter
Demonstrate safe property mutation
hints: Partial<T> allows passing subset objects containing any number of optional properties
exercises.codeExample: type Draft = Partial<Article>;

exercises.title: Utility Types: Pick, Omit & Record
exercises.description: Construct new interface models using Pick<T, K>, Omit<T, K>, and Record<K, T>.
exercises.theory: Pick extracts specific keys from a type. Omit constructs a type by removing keys. Record<K, T> maps property keys to value types.
exercises.objective: Derive UserPreview using Pick, CreateUserDTO using Omit, and a UserRoleMap using Record.
requirements: Derive UserPreview type using Pick<User, 'id' | 'name'>
Derive CreateUserDTO using Omit<User, 'id' | 'passwordHash'>
Create RolePermissions map with Record<K, T>
hints: Omit is ideal for creation DTOs that exclude server-generated IDs
exercises.codeExample: type DTO = Omit<User, 'id'>; type Map = Record<string, number>;

exercises.title: Mapped Types & Index Signatures
exercises.description: Dynamically transform object properties using mapped types and string index signatures.
exercises.theory: Mapped types ([K in keyof T]) iterate over type keys to produce modified property specifications. Index signatures ([key: string]: value) handle dynamic dictionary objects.
exercises.objective: Build a ReadonlyMapped<T> type and dynamic Dictionary interface.
requirements: Create mapped type ReadonlyMapped<T> using keyof T
Create StringDictionary with string index signature [key: string]: string
hints: keyof T generates a union of all property keys in type T
exercises.codeExample: type Nullable<T> = { [P in keyof T]: T[P] | null };

exercises.title: Conditional Types & infer Keyword
exercises.description: Evaluate type relationships conditionally using T extends U ? X : Y and infer type parameters.
exercises.theory: Conditional types select output types based on subtype testing. The infer keyword declares type variables within condition expressions.
exercises.objective: Create an UnpackArray<T> conditional type.
requirements: Write conditional type UnpackArray<T>
Use infer U inside array pattern matching
hints: infer captures array element types dynamically
exercises.codeExample: type ElementType<T> = T extends (infer U)[] ? U : T;

exercises.title: Template Literal Types
exercises.description: Construct strongly-typed string patterns using template literal types.
exercises.theory: Template literal types generate string unions by interpolating other types into literal template positions.
exercises.objective: Build an EventName template literal type combining Entity and Action names.
requirements: Define Entity and Action literal string unions
Construct EventName using template literal syntax `${Entity}_${Action}`
Demonstrate compile-time type safety
hints: EventName evaluates automatically to 'user_created' | 'user_deleted' | 'post_created' | 'post_deleted'
exercises.codeExample: type Event = `${Topic}:${Action}`;

exercises.title: TypeScript Decorators
exercises.description: Annotate classes and methods using experimental/standard decorators.
exercises.theory: Decorators provide meta-programming capabilities to wrap class definitions, methods, or parameters with reusable behaviors.
exercises.objective: Write a method execution logger decorator pattern.
requirements: Create method decorator target function
Wrap originalMethod and log execution parameters
hints: Decorators receive target class prototype, propertyKey name, and propertyDescriptor
exercises.codeExample: function Log(target: any, key: string) {}

exercises.title: Declaration Files (.d.ts) & Ambient Typing
exercises.description: Write custom declaration files (.d.ts) and declare global ambient module interfaces.
exercises.theory: Declaration files (.d.ts) supply TypeScript type specifications for un-typed third-party JavaScript libraries or global environments.
exercises.objective: Write ambient module declaration for an untyped library.
requirements: Write declare global interface extension for Window
Include string property BYTECODE_VERSION
hints: declare global allows augmenting built-in environment interfaces like Window or Process
exercises.codeExample: declare global { interface Window { custom: boolean; } }

exercises.title: Strict Null Checks & Non-Null Assertion (!)
exercises.description: Handle strictNullChecks configuration, nullish coalescing, and non-null assertion operator (!).
exercises.theory: strictNullChecks prevents unexpected null pointer crashes. The non-null assertion operator (!) asserts to the compiler that a value is non-null.
exercises.objective: Handle nullable DOM query elements safely.
exercises.initialCode:
const input = document.getElementById('search');
// Safely access value
requirements: Type HTMLInputElement | null for document query
Use optional chaining and nullish coalescing for safe access
hints: Avoid over-using non-null assertion operator !; prefer runtime checks
exercises.codeExample: const val = input?.value ?? 'default';

exercises.title: TypeScript with Async REST API Architecture
exercises.description: Build end-to-end typed REST client wrapper with generic HTTP methods.
exercises.theory: Combining generics with async/await creates type-safe API clients where response types are enforced at call sites.
exercises.objective: Build a typed ApiClient class with generic get and post methods.
requirements: Build ApiClient class with private baseUrl field
Implement generic method get<T>(endpoint: string): Promise<T>
hints: Returning Promise<T> enforces type checking when calling code awaits client.get<UserData>()
exercises.codeExample: async get<T>(url: string): Promise<T> {}

exercises.title: Capstone Project: Type-Safe Command CLI Task Engine
exercises.description: Engineer a complete Type-Safe Command Task Engine utilizing Generics, Interfaces, Discriminated Unions, Utility Types, and Enums.
exercises.theory: This capstone exercise synthesizes TypeScript's type system: Generic repositories, interfaces, discriminated union commands, Enums, and Pick/Omit utility types into a cohesive CLI task management architecture.
exercises.objective: Construct a complete Type-Safe Task Engine.
requirements: Declare TaskStatus Enum
Define Task interface with readonly id
Derive CreateTaskDTO using Omit<Task, 'id'>
Implement TaskEngine class with type-safe methods
hints: Combine Omit for payload input DTOs with Enum filtering
exercises.codeExample: class Engine { tasks: Task[] = []; }

references.title: TypeScript Official Handbook
references.description: Comprehensive reference documentation for TypeScript features and configuration
